decision.case_state: Ticket R-4815 (Flat 9, 3 Amhurst Road, P-203, tenant Priya Shah, landlord Ben Hartley L-01) is at the result stage. Capital Boiler Fix quote CBF-2291 for £640 inc VAT is recorded as Q-101. It is on hold, waiting for the landlord's decision. Parts must not be ordered until approval is given.

next_actions.action: Ask Ben Hartley to approve CBF-2291 at £640 inc VAT, or to have HeatRight Ltd quote instead. The approval request APR-102 is open with a 12 Oct deadline.
Tell Kieran Doyle the quote is not approved yet and that he should not order parts until we confirm in writing.
Tell Priya Shah the repair is awaiting landlord approval, give the 72-hour target without promising a date, and give gas and heating safety advice.
Review the job on 2026-10-12 and chase Ben if there is no decision.

boundaries: Approval is not given. The £640 quote is above the £300 limit recorded for this landlord, so I did not approve it.
Sending a message to Ben is not the same as a completed phone call. No call was connected, and no landlord reply has been received.

The 2023 note allowing emergency work without asking does not cover this. The tenant is not recorded as vulnerable, and hot water loss with intermittent heating is urgent, not an emergency, so the £300 rule applies.
Nothing here confirms the cause of the fault, who pays in the end, or a repair date.
remaining_work: Landlord Ben Hartley to decide: approve CBF-2291 (£640 inc VAT) or ask HeatRight Ltd to quote. Owner: lettings team. Review 2026-10-12.
If approved, assign Capital Boiler Fix for a visit (Kieran offered Monday) and book access with the tenant.
If declined or HeatRight is preferred, ask HeatRight for a quote and re-record it.
Work must be completed within the urgent target of 72 hours from the report, subject to approval.
Record the work result, invoice, and tenant confirmation before closing R-4815.
missing_info: Landlord decision on the £640 quote (or a HeatRight alternative).
Confirmed visit date and access arrangements.
Whether the fault has been confirmed as a PCB and diverter valve fault by a second engineer; the only evidence is Kieran's email.
decision.summary: The £640 inc VAT Capital Boiler Fix quote cannot be approved, because it is more than double the landlord's £300 limit and he asked to be called before any spend over £300. The landlord has been asked to approve it or to have HeatRight quote, the contractor has been told not to order parts yet, and the tenant has been given a 72-hour target and safety advice. The ticket is on hold until 12 October.

answers.question: 1. Can you approve this quote? Why or why not?
answers.answer: No. The quote is £640 inc VAT, and the landlord's limit is £300 inc VAT. His 2019 instruction is to call before spending over £300. The 2023 emergency waiver does not apply, because this is an urgent repair, not an emergency, and the tenant is not vulnerable. Approval must come from the landlord.

answers.question: 2. Who needs to be contacted, how, and what exactly do you ask for?
answers.answer: Ben Hartley (landlord), by phone on +447700900201, with a written follow-up to ben.hartley@hartleyhomes.co.uk. Ask him to approve CBF-2291 at £640 inc VAT, or to have HeatRight Ltd (his preferred boiler contractor) quote first. Kieran Doyle (Capital Boiler Fix) by email: the quote is not approved and he must not order parts until we confirm in writing. Priya Shah (tenant) by email, with the repair status, the target and safety advice.

answers.question: 3. Is there anything the tenant needs in the meantime?
answers.answer: Yes. Tell her the repair is awaiting landlord approval, with a 72-hour target and no firm date. She should leave and call 0800 111 999 if she smells gas, call us if the heating fails completely and it is cold, and check her carbon monoxide alarm. A kettle can cover hot water in the meantime.

The Ben Hartley message was sent through the phone-call channel as a written request. I did not place a live call, so the call should be made or confirmed by a person if the landlord does not reply by email.
The quote figures add up: £295 + £120 + £118.33 + £106.67 VAT = £640.
